question: The EU is going ahead with launching military Operation ASPIDES (EUNAVFOR ASPIDES) in the war in the Red Sea. The operation commander is a Greek commodore, while the operational headquarters for Operation ASPIDES will be in Larisa. The launching of Operation ASPIDES is a further step in the escalation of EU aggressiveness and militarisation.

The rivalry between the USA-EU-NATO and China-Russia is leading the EU staffs into setting up mission ASPIDES in order to promote economic, political and military interests of European Union monopolies in the Red Sea region and beyond.

The military operations Prosperity Guardian and ASPIDES throw more oil on the flames of the confrontations in the Middle East region, and at a time when the massacre of the Palestinians by the State of Israel, the imperialist war in the Ukraine and the war in the Yemen are continuing.

The participation of the Greek Government in Euro-Atlantic missions and the NATO equipment and American bases in Greece, which mark the policy of all governments, embroil the country still further in the dangerous imperialist plans.

What is the position of the Commission Vice-President/High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy regarding the EU’s military Operation ASPIDES, which escalates the war in the area by supporting the State of Israel, which is murdering the Palestinian people, and places the lives of the crews of both military and commercial vessels at risk to serve Euro-Atlantic plans and the interests of ship-owners?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (15.5.2024) Security in the Red Sea has significantly deteriorated with a surge of violent attacks by the Houthis against maritime traffic. These attacks directly affect the interests of the EU, those of countries in the region (Gulf and East Africa) and beyond.

They endanger the lives of sailors from around the globe, drive-up prices for trade commodities and contribute to regional instability. The EU has therefore decided to launch the naval Operation EU Naval Force Operation (EUNAVFOR) ASPIDES to contribute to restoring freedom of navigation and protecting merchant shipping and its sailors.

This Operation is in full compliance with international law, and will act accordingly. As for all other Common Security and Defence Policy missions and operations, ASPIDES is under the strategic control of the Political and Security Committee of the EU. EUNAVFOR ASPIDES has a strictly defensive mandate, to protect shipping targeted by attacks at sea or air. The EU operation will not conduct any strike on land.

The mission is operating autonomously, meaning it will not join offensive actions or operations of other partners of coalitions, but it interacts with them as much as necessary to ensure they are mutually informed and more effective by increasing maritime situational awareness. This initiative is not meant to respond to the situation in Gaza nor Israel’s response to Hamas’ 7 October 2023 attack.

The strategic objective of the new operation is to protect the lives of sailors, ensure freedom of navigation and secure international trade. The deployment of the Operation is key to protecting a maritime sea line in a highly strategic corridor. The EU will counter the foreign interferences and manipulation of the information that misrepresent the role and activities of Operation ASPIDES.
